subject: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 17, 2026 at 4:12 PM -0800
Subject: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

Evelyn,

We’re asking for exec approval on the GA target date + comms plan for the Console “Usage Insights: cost drivers by route” project.

Proposed GA target: Thu, Apr 9, 2026
- Beta continues with design partners + internal dogfooding through mid/late March
- GA gating criteria remains: API p95 + freshness SLOs green, export job success rate stable, and cardinality alarms within budget

Quick status
- Route + model dimensions: implemented end-to-end behind flag (Hosted + Dedicated; Private requires customer upgrade path—docs callout)
- Console UI: route list + route detail in staging; export action wired to job service
- Security: audit events spec reviewed; RBAC enforcement in progress (Kaitlyn + Kevin are tracking)

Top risks (and our mitigation)
1) Cardinality (route naming explosion)
   - Mitigation: normalization + length limits + reserved “unknown/other”; hard caps per org/project + alarms
   - DevEx: route naming guidance + SDK defaults to avoid dynamic IDs
2) Export performance/timeouts (large ranges)
   - Mitigation: max time window + row caps; async job; retry + backoff; explicit UX when the request is truncated; audit logs on create/download
3) Invoice reconciliation / customer confusion
   - Mitigation: consistent messaging in-product ("near real-time" + late-arriving metering), FAQ + support macros (Dev Patel has the draft)

Requested decisions
A) Approve Apr 9 GA date for planning (release notes + internal enablement)
B) Approve comms plan: blog + docs + in-console banner for existing orgs, and a short internal one-pager (Sales/CS) to address export/audit questions (ties to INT-913)

Attachments:
- UsageInsights_GA_Readiness_2026-02-18.pdf
- GA_Comms_OnePager_UsageInsights_2026-02-18.docx

Thanks,
Marissa
Director of Product, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 17, 2026 at 5:03 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

Thanks. A few questions before I sign off:

1) What is our current measured export job failure rate in staging under load, and what’s the worst-case runtime for the max window?
2) Are we confident RBAC/audit logging is “done” for GA (no follow-up work that would make us walk back claims in a security review)?
3) If route cardinality spikes for a single org, what’s the customer-visible behavior? (silent rollup vs hard rejection vs delayed reporting)

If we can answer those crisply + document the GA gates, I’m aligned on the April window.

Evelyn


From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 17, 2026 at 6:01 PM -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

Jumping in on (1) + (3).

(1) Export performance (staging load test as of today)
- Max window proposal: 31 days (hourly rollups), with a hard row cap (we’re tuning, current target is 250k rows)
- With those limits, p95 export job completion: 2m 40s; p99: 4m 55s
- Failure rate over ~1,200 jobs: 0.6% (primarily timeouts when we intentionally exceeded limits); within-limits failures were 0.1% and were retried successfully
- We’ll continue to run nightly load on export service and add an alert at >1% failures rolling 30m

(3) Cardinality behavior
- We’re not hard-rejecting requests for new routes (we don’t want customers to see inference failures due to analytics tagging)
- Pipeline behavior when an org/project exceeds the budget: newly-seen route values are normalized and then rolled into “other” for aggregations; raw route string may be hashed for auditing/debug but will not show as a distinct dimension
- Customer-visible behavior: the “other” bucket grows + a banner in the route list when we detect excessive unique routes (“Route tagging exceeds recommended limits; see naming guidance”). Support macro will point to the docs.

We’ll include the GA gates as a checklist in the release coordination doc; Connor is adding it to the release train.

Logan
EM, Telemetry & Analytics Platform


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 8:22 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

On (2) RBAC + audit logging readiness:

- RBAC: the plan is strict org/project scoping enforced at the Insights API layer and again in export job creation (deny-by-default). We’re adding integration tests to prevent cross-project leakage.
- Audit logging: export job create + download events will be emitted with actor, org/project, time range, filters (route/model/region/env), result size, and job ID. Retention follows standard audit log retention.
- GA claims: We can confidently say “exports are audit-logged” and “insights respect project boundaries” once ENG-8428 + the security checklist sign-off is completed.

Remaining work:
- One final security review pass on the exact event fields (no customer prompt payloads in audit logs; only report metadata)
- A doc snippet for Security/Compliance to reference in questionnaires (ties to INT-913)

I’m comfortable with the plan, with the condition that we don’t flip GA flag broadly until the tests are merged and we complete the checklist.

Marcus
Security Engineering


From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paula Mendes <paula_mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:11 AM -0800
Subject: Re: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

Approved to plan for GA on Thu, Apr 9, 2026.

Conditions:
- GA gate checklist must explicitly include: (a) RBAC integration tests merged, (b) audit event fields finalized + validated in prod, (c) export job failure rate <1% within limits for 7 consecutive days, and (d) documented customer-visible behavior for cardinality rollup.
- Comms: approved, but keep the first blog/docs messaging tight on limitations (freshness, max export window, and that route accuracy depends on tagging).

Connor: please align this with the April console release train and add a “no-go” owner for each gate.

Evelyn

Subject: Re: Exec approval: Usage Insights (Cost drivers by route) GA date + comms plan

Got it—thank you.

Next steps:
- Connor/Paula will publish the GA gating checklist today with owners + target dates (we’ll attach it to PM-612 and link from the release notes draft)
- Marcus + Kevin will finalize the audit event fields this week; we’ll include the INT-913 one-pager updates in the comms pack
- Logan/Allison will wire the export failure-rate + lag alerts into the rollout dashboard and confirm the 7-day burn-in criteria

We’ll keep the external messaging explicit about limits and dependencies (tagging + retention/freshness).

Marissa
